intent: A number that keeps climbing: a THEN/NOW split puts 153 centenarians in 1963 against today while the counter runs to 99,000, per-person bars show why China's billion does not win, and a pin lands on the island famous for long lives with the silver-cup card.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country has the MOST people aged 100 or more?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country has the most people aged 100 or more?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Japan. Nearly 100,000 people who have passed their hundredth birthday.

lines.direction: ease back so the whole archipelago sits in frame; the THEN/NOW split slides in on 'count' — 153 against 99,000+; a cake sticker on 'count'; the counter runs to 99,000 from 'today' to 'women'; a grandmother sticker on 'women' as Japan pulses
lines.text: When the count began in 1963, there were 153. Today it is around 99,000, mostly women.

lines.direction: hold wide; the Chinese flag-ball thinks on 'China' with a crowd sticker; three per-person bars rise on 'person' with Japan towering; a US flag-ball thinks on 'America' as Japan pulses
lines.text: China has far more people, but per person Japan has about 80 centenarians per 100,000. America has around 30.

lines.direction: push south-west to the islands; the Okinawa pin and tag land on 'Okinawa' with a palm sticker; the SILVER CUP card and a trophy sticker on 'cup'; the Japanese flag-ball grins on 'many' with a money-bag sticker as Japan pulses; pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Okinawa is the famous island of long lives. The government once sent every new centenarian a silver cup, until there were too many.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
